daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Partai Solidaritas Indonesia (PSI) addressed speculation about its activities amid coalition dynamics, with party spokesperson Isyana stating the party is focused on forming structures rather than recruiting PDI-P cadres. Separately, PSI confirmed that former President Jokowi will begin regional tours but did not specify timing. An analyst discussed the prospects of Cabinet Secretary Teddy as a potential vice-presidential candidate for Prabowo in 2029.

  • Komnas HAM released findings of alleged human rights violations in the MBG program and issued nine recommendations, with former Constitutional Court chief Busyro Muqoddas calling for the program to be temporarily halted due to lack of transparency.
  • Vice President Gibran acknowledged his own shortcomings before students and urged them to continue improving their capabilities related to artificial intelligence.
  • Former Coordinating Minister Mahfud MD stated he doubted the government's commitment to police reform from the outset and criticized presidential intervention in the Tom Lembong and Hasto cases as dangerous for the future of law.
  • DPR Commission III member Rieke Dyah Pitaloka called on the government to adjust budget allocations for the Witness and Victim Protection Agency (LPSK).
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Public Works and Housing plan to revise the definition of low-income households and remove domicile barriers to support the 3 million homes program.
  • The National Audit Agency (BGN) announced it will fully audit free meal kitchens during the school holidays.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, with the visit described as marking a new phase in Indonesia-Germany relations. Prabowo underscored the importance of cooperation with Berlin, while the two countries also signed agreements to deepen trade and clean energy partnerships.

  • Cabinet Secretary Teddy Indra Wijaya met with the Indian ambassador to discuss Prime Minister Modi's planned mid-year visit to Jakarta next month.
  • The Indonesian business chamber HIPMI announced its support for deeper Indonesia-Germany trade and investment ties amid Steinmeier's state visit.
  • Maluku province explored potential cooperation with France in education and tourism sectors.
  • The Agency for the Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers (KP2MI) announced it is monitoring the handling of Indonesian workers in Taiwan.

Other

A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck Central Sulawesi's Palu, prompting authorities to launch an emergency response. The disaster left one person dead and 13 seriously injured, with 109 people affected according to disaster agency BNPB. The communications ministry reported that eight mobile phone towers have been restored following the quake.

  • Finance Minister Purbaya stated that the easing of US-Iran tensions opens additional fiscal space in the state budget.
  • The Indonesia Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs (INDEF) urged the government to maintain fiscal discipline to sustain the rupiah and Jakarta Composite Index rally.
  • The government allocated Rp9.7 trillion for village electrification in the 2027 budget.
  • Indonesia aims to establish 100 ecosystem work payment schemes this year to support environmental conservation.
  • The Jakarta provincial government will seek Singaporean investment for MRT expansion phases in the capital.
